newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindustan Lever drags down Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Hindustan Lever drags down Delhi shares.

text.p: Most blue chips reversed early losses and ended higher in mixed trade on Thursday but a sharp fall in Hindustan Lever Ltd pushed the benchmark index to a lower close on the Delhi bourse, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 2.63 points lower at 780.60 points.
Hindustan Lever plunged 18.50 rupees, or 1.83 percent, to 990.50 as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) unloaded their stakes in the company ahead of the fiscal year-end, brokers said.
March 31 is the last day of the 1996/97 financial year.
Brokers said they did not expect the recovery in other share prices to last long.
"The late recovery in share prices seems to be temporary and was attributed to low-level buying," said Yogesh Sethi of brokers Vinayaka Investments.
"The market should react further in coming sessions as operators might square up their positions before the financial year closes," Sethi added.
Traders said most blue chips erased their losses as FIIs stepped up buying and speculators squared their positions.
State Bank of India ended 2.80 rupees higher at 311.45.
